overview: Ward-level QI project over the 2026 to 2027 bronchiolitis season: weekly baseline points from the previous season's charts, then three PDSA cycles introducing and refining a direct-cessation weaning protocol for infants aged 8 weeks or older.
population: Infants aged 8 weeks or older with bronchiolitis on high-flow nasal cannula on the general pediatric ward; infants under 8 weeks continue stepwise weaning and are followed descriptively.
exposure: Once stable for two hours in FiO2 of 40 percent or less, high flow is stopped with a trial off; restart criteria are fixed in protocol version 1.2. A plain-language criteria card is given to parents.
procedures: Cycle 1 (November): day shifts only. Cycle 2 (December to January): 24 hours, with a fixed 22:00 assessment added if night trials off lag. Cycle 3 (February to March): refinements from cycle reviews. A bedside log records trial-off time, restarts and missed checks; the weekly run chart is reviewed at the ward huddle; the PICU lead reviews every re-escalation.

outcomes.name: Time on high flow
outcomes.measure: Weekly median hours from high-flow start to final stop for infants aged 8 weeks or older
outcomes.timing: Weekly, baseline season and November to March
outcomes.why: The outcome families notice and the protocol targets (claims c1, c2).

outcomes.name: Re-escalation within 24 hours
outcomes.measure: Proportion of trials off followed by restarting high flow within 24 hours

outcomes.name: PICU transfer or readmission within 7 days
outcomes.measure: Count of PICU transfers within 48 hours of stopping and readmissions within 7 days of discharge
outcomes.why: Serious harms the protocol must not increase.

outcomes.name: Protocol adherence
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible infants with a trial off within two hours of meeting criteria, by day and night
outcomes.why: Night delivery is the weak link (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Length of stay
outcomes.measure: Weekly median hours from ward admission to discharge
outcomes.why: Shorter high flow should shorten stays.

feasibility: About 100 to 120 infants on high flow in a season; the bedside log adds under a minute per check; the run chart uses chart data the ward already records.
biasMitigation: Operational definitions of trial off and restart fixed before November
Run chart annotated with viral season peaks and staffing changes
Every re-escalation reviewed by the PICU lead
Infants under 8 weeks followed descriptively as a separate group

biasFlags.label: Season severity
biasFlags.note: A severe season lengthens stays whatever the protocol; annotated on the chart.

biasFlags.label: Selective use of the protocol
biasFlags.note: Attendings may exclude sicker infants; exclusions are logged with reasons.

biasFlags.label: Unmeasured readmissions elsewhere
biasFlags.note: 7-day phone call asks about other hospitals.

flags: Two safety balancing measures carry the stopping rule
parsimony.simplestPath: One protocol, one run chart, safety balancing measures, three cycles.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement; no additional framework.
summary: Three PDSA cycles with one primary outcome, two safety balancing measures, one process measure and length of stay.
